jobs.description:
Job Title: Chair, Division of Business and Leadership

Reporting Relationship:Dean of DeVoe School of Business, Technology, and Leadership

Unit: National & Global

Department: DBTL Business Division Admin-National & Global

Campus Location: Online/Remote

Summary of Position:The Chair, Division of Business and Leadership is a full-time, 12-month administrative faculty position in the DeVoe School of Business, Technology, and Leadership (DBTL), within the College of Adult and Professional Studies (CAPS). The Chair provides strategic leadership for all degree programs in the division, working closely with faculty to set direction, develop curriculum, and build new programs.

The Chair supervises and develops the division's faculty and staff, manages the division budget, and serves as the final escalation point for faculty and student concerns. For undergraduate programs, the Chair owns curriculum and faculty, and the Director, Undergraduate Program Success owns retention and student experience.

The Chair also drives specific programs, serving as program director for the master's business programs: the Master of Business Administration (MBA), the Executive MBA (EMBA), and the Master of Science in Management (MSM). In that role, the Chair leads curriculum decisions so each program stays relevant to the market. Course development and other execution run through the School's curriculum systems.


Duties and Responsibilities

  • Supervise and develop division faculty
    • Supervise and mentor the full-time faculty of the Division of Business and Leadership, including an assistant professor who leads the division's bachelor's and master's leadership programs
    • Build a collaborative faculty culture in which faculty own and steward the curriculum
    • Supervise the Coordinator of Affiliate Faculty, who oversees adjunct faculty directly
    • Serve as the final escalation point for adjunct and student concerns. Adjunct concerns go first to the Coordinator of Affiliate Faculty, who works with the Chair as needed. Student concerns move from the course faculty member to their affiliate faculty, then to the Coordinator of Affiliate Faculty, and to the Chair if needed
    • Conduct annual reviews in cooperation with the Dean, guide professional development plans, and support faculty through rank advancement
    • Coordinate full-time faculty teaching assignments for the academic year, and promote faculty research and service
  • Lead division strategy, curriculum, and new programs
    • Set the strategic vision and goals for the division's undergraduate and graduate programs with division faculty, and carry them through implementation
    • Coordinate curriculum development across the division, and lead curriculum decisions for the undergraduate programs
    • Partner with the Associate Dean for Doctoral Programs and the Chair, Division of Technology, so content leadership follows expertise across reporting lines, especially in leadership and technology
    • Use market and enrollment data to decide where the division's programs should grow or adapt
    • Identify new program ideas and expand the division's offerings. Work with the Dean to move them through the College and University approval process
  • Direct curriculum for the MBA, EMBA, and MSM
    • Serve as program director for the MBA, EMBA, and MSM, and lead curriculum decisions for each program
    • Keep the programs relevant to the market. Track employer needs, competitor programs, and enrollment trends, and turn those findings into curriculum changes
    • Keep the curriculum grounded in ethical, Christ-centered leadership. Give the EMBA a distinct design for experienced executives
    • Set direction for course development and revision, working with the Director of Curriculum Operations and the School's course development systems to carry it out
    • Partner with SEP and IWU Marketing so program positioning reflects what makes each program distinct
  • Ensure academic quality, assessment, and accreditation
    • Ensure division programs operate in line with the academic policies of the School, College, and University and the standards of accrediting bodies, including HLC and ACBSP
    • Lead the annual assessment of each division program. Report the results and a strategic plan to the Office of Academic Assessment and Evaluation and to the Dean
    • Work with the Director of Curriculum Operations and ACBSP accreditation staff on reporting and course revisions
  • Partner on student success and program data
    • Partner with the Director, Undergraduate Program Success. The Chair owns curriculum and faculty; the Director owns retention, progression, and the student experience. The two share responsibility for outcomes
    • Use enrollment, retention, and program health data from the Executive Director, Strategy & Insights in planning and program review
  • Own the division budget, enrollment, and revenue goals
    • Prepare and manage the division budget, with a focus on meeting revenue goals and minimizing expenses
    • Work closely with Strategic Enrollment & Partnerships (SEP) and IWU Marketing on marketing and recruiting for division programs
  • Serve the School and connect the division externally
    • Serve on School, College, University, ad hoc, and standing committees and councils as required
    • Attend school, college and N&G meetings as required and commencement exercises
    • Build relationships with employers and professional organizations that strengthen the master's programs, coordinating with the School's partnership efforts
    • Contribute division expertise to the School's thought leadership, events, and advisory council work
  • Maintain scholarship, service, and faith integration
    • As administrative faculty (Faculty Handbook 3.2.1.4), maintain an active scholarly agenda in the Chair's discipline. Scholarship focuses on the discipline, seeks answers to real questions, is open to review, and results in a public product (Faculty Handbook 3.4.5)
    • Set annual expectations for scholarship and service with the Dean through the Annual Review & Goal Development process, which covers faith, teaching, scholarship, and service (CAPS Supplement II.C)
    • Teaching is not a standing expectation. The Dean may assign a teaching load, in consultation with the CAPS Vice President of Academic Affairs (CAPS Supplement II.A)
  • Perform other responsibilities as assigned

Qualifications:According to Indiana Wesleyan University employment policy all employees must possess a strong Christian commitment and adhere to the standards outlined in the IWU Community Lifestyle Statement.

Education

  • Earned doctorate (PhD, DBA, or equivalent) from a regionally accredited institution in business, management, leadership, or a closely related field

Experience

  • Required Experience
    • A substantial record of effective teaching at the college level
    • Significant leadership experience, measured by both length of service and level of responsibility, including supervising faculty
    • Curriculum development and program assessment experience
    • An active scholarship agenda that includes research, publications, presentations, and service
    • Budget management experience tied to enrollment and revenue goals
    • A strong commitment to the University's mission and to Christ-centered higher education
  • Preferred experience
    • Program leadership in graduate business programs, or comparable leadership in another key content area of the division
    • Experience with Business School and/or Regional accreditation
    • Executive or professional business experience outside academia, which strengthens EMBA credibility
    • Eligibility for appointment at the rank of associate professor or above

Required Skills

  • Demonstrated ability to lead faculty, build shared direction, and manage change
  • Demonstrated ability to read market and enrollment data and translate it into program decisions
  • Demonstrated teaching ability, specifically with adult learners in online and hybrid formats
  • Demonstrated knowledge of online educational delivery tools, including Brightspace
  • Demonstrated proficiency with Microsoft Office products

IWU Kingdom Diversity Statement

IWU, in covenant with God's reconciling work and in accordance with the Biblical principles of our historic Wesleyan tradition, commits to build a community that reflects Kingdom diversity. We will foster an intentional environment for living, teaching and learning, which exhibits honor, respect, and dignity. Acknowledging visible or invisible differences, our community authentically values each member's earthly and eternal worth. We refute ignorance and isolation and embrace deliberate and courageous engagement that exhibits Christ's commandment to love all humankind.

LIMITATIONS AND DISCLAIMER

As a religious educational institution operating under the auspices of The Wesleyan Church, Indiana Wesleyan University is permitted and reserves the right to prefer employees on the basis of religion (42 U.S.C., Sections 2000e-1 and 2000e-2).

Employees will be required to follow other job-related instructions and to perform other job-related duties requested by their supervisor in compliance with Federal and State Laws.

Homestead Studio
We are an email marketing agency specializing in growing eCommerce brands by creating exciting, engaging, and personalized messaging across email and SMS channels. Our expertise in email and SMS marketing allows our clients to cultivate relationships with potential customers and build lasting relationships with current customers to create lifetime value.

About the role

Client Success at Homestead is about two things. First, giving our teams what they need to own their clients' outcomes and do their best work. Second, making sure every brand we work with has the best experience possible, with someone in their corner who listens, advocates for them, and makes things right when they go sideways. In this role, you're that person for both.

As our Client Success Manager, you'll be the person our DTC clients and delivery teams turn to when a relationship gets hard. You'll cover a portfolio of about 30 brands across email & SMS and paid social, and most weeks bring a handful of urgent issues that need same-day attention.

Your job is to figure out what's really going wrong, fix it with the team, and make sure the fix holds. We'll train you on how our email and paid work gets made, so you can explain what's happening to a founder plainly and honestly. You'll work closely with our leadership team and have the chance to lead communication and other training to share your expertise with the wider team. This isn't a sales or renewal role.

Responsibilities

  • Escalations. Take in urgent issues from clients and the team, separate facts from assumptions, and build a fix rather than passing the problem along.
  • Client resets. Lead issue and reset calls with founders and marketing leads and turn scattered feedback into one point of contact and one combined revision round.
  • Key moments. Open and close every creative kickoff and check in one month after kickoff and two weeks after any team change.
  • Team transitions. Guide clients through strategist and account manager changes so important context isn't lost.
  • Portfolio health. Keep our client tracker current, reach out to quiet accounts, and run a post-mortem whenever a client leaves.
  • Team support. Catch workload concerns early, spot patterns across weeks, and raise staffing or scope issues with leadership.
  • Clear updates. After each touchpoint, send a recap to the client, to leadership and to the account team.
  • Training. Lead communication training for strategists, designers, copywriters and account managers to improve the team as you spot patterns.

    • Gather project requirements, analyze resource needs, and create comprehensive project estimates and formal proposals (Statement of Work).

    • Establish clear timelines, deliverables, and budget caps with clients prior to project kick-off.

    • Conduct regular status updates with clients to ensure expectations, timelines, and satisfaction align with project goals.

  2. Team Oversight & Time Tracking Management

    • Monitor day-to-day team allocation and work progress to ensure deliverables stay on schedule.

    • Enforce time-tracking protocols across internal teams, ensuring hours are logged accurately against correct project codes daily/weekly.

    • Review and approve team timesheets, verifying that logged hours reflect actual work performed with the internal team heads.

    • Identify resource bottlenecks early and adjust project schedules or resource assignments accordingly.

  3. Financial Oversight, Scope Control & Billing

  • Track real-time project spend against approved budgets to catch overages before they occur.

  • Identify scope creep promptly, draft change orders, negotiate additional budget with clients, and gain approval before additional work begins.

  • Reconcile logged billable hours, expense receipts, and milestone completions to prepare monthly/project-based billing reports.

  • Work closely with the accounting/finance team to generate precise invoices and resolve any billing discrepancies with clients.

4. Quality Assurance & Continuous Improvement

  • Conduct post-project reviews (post-mortems) to measure final profitability against initial estimates.

  • Analyze historical time and cost data to continuously refine future budget estimation models.

  • Maintain high client retention rates by proactively identifying issues and delivering excellent service quality.

Requirements

Mandatory Requirements & Qualifications

  • Experience: 3–5+ years in project management, operations management, or client account management within a professional services, agency, consulting, or technical service environment.

  • Financial Acumen: Proven experience creating project budgets, tracking billable hours, and managing burn rates/profit margins.

  • Software Proficiency: Hands-on experience with time-tracking and project management tools and invoicing software.

  • Communication: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills with a track record of handling high-value client relationships.

  • Leadership: Strong team-coordination skills with the ability to hold team members accountable for process adherence without sacrificing morale.

  • Problem-Solving: Strong analytical capability to spot financial variances, resolve client concerns, and streamline operational workflows.

Purpose

To lead the international, comprehensive lifespan Our Whole Lives Sexuality Education (OWL) and Sexuality and Our Faith (SoF) program in partnership with the United Church of Christ (UCC); to oversee curriculum and resource development that supports congregations in providing developmentally appropriate, medically accurate, justice-centered sexuality education; to manage facilitator and trainer training; to expand the use of OWL into new markets; and to represent the UUA as a leader in faith-based sexuality education.

Principal Responsibilities

1. Lead the planning, funding, revision, and development of Our Whole Lives (OWL) and Sexuality and Our Faith (SoF) curricula and resources in partnership with the United Church of Christ (UCC), ensuring materials remain relevant, effective, and aligned with program goals.
2. Contract and oversee authors, project managers, artists, editors, and reviewers; coordinate developmental editing, field testing, accessibility review, and accountability review processes for new and revised resources.
3. Establish, maintain, and evaluate standards for OWL facilitator and trainer preparation, certification, performance, and continuing education in collaboration with UCC partners.
4. Manage the OWL trainer network; coordinate annual facilitator training schedules; oversee trainer agreements and background checks; and plan and co-lead Training of Trainers events and ongoing trainer development opportunities.
5. Supervise the OWL Administrator and provide leadership for the effective administration, implementation, and continuous improvement of OWL programs and services.
6. Oversee program budgets, contracts, cost-sharing agreements, policy implementation, participant safety practices, data systems, and operational processes supporting OWL and SoF programs.
7. Maintain OWL-related web content and communications; oversee webinars and outreach initiatives; respond to inquiries; and promote OWL through presentations, trainings, media opportunities, and other public engagement activities.
8. Provide consultation and guidance on sexuality education, OWL implementation, facilitator practices, and emerging trends in the field; participate in ongoing professional development to maintainexpertise.
9. Represent the UUA in partnership and governance relationships related to OWL, including collaboration with the UCC, Canadian Unitarian Council, United Methodist Church, legal counsel, and other stakeholders.
10. Convene and support the OWL Advisory Council and engage key stakeholders, partners, and volunteers to strengthen program effectiveness, sustainability, and strategic direction.

11. Perform other duties as requested by supervisor, the Vice Presidents, or the President.

Qualifications

This position has a salary midpoint of $80,900. Compensation may vary based on factors such as experience, qualifications, and geographical location, with offers potentially ranging 10-15% higher or lower than the midpoint.Requirements include:

Qualifications

  • Five or more years of professional experience in sexuality education or a related field; graduate-level study or degree preferred.
  • Deep familiarity with the curriculum and philosophy of Our Whole Lives (OWL), religious education, and/or reproductive and gender justice work.
  • Demonstrated commitment to inclusive, medically accurate, developmentally appropriate sexuality education. Experience as an OWL trainer or facilitator preferred.
  • Experience developing, revising, or managing curricula, training materials, and educational resources.
  • Strong program and project management skills, including budget oversight, contractor management, and coordination of multiple priorities.
  • Excellent written, verbal, facilitation, and public communication skills, including the ability to navigate sensitive or controversial topics.
  • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively, build partnerships, exercise sound judgment, and balance initiative with appropriate consultation and accountability.
  • Understanding of Unitarian Universalist theology, congregational life, and the mission of the UUA
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Google Workspace; supervisory and cross-organizational partnership experience preferred
  • Understanding of issues around anti-racism, anti-oppression, and multiculturalism
  • Work or lived experience with BIPOC communities is ofparticular value
  • Eagerness to work in an organization in which the dismantling of white supremacy is a high priority

How to Apply

People with disabilities, people of color, indigenous people, Hispanic/Latinx, and LGBTQ candidates are encouraged to apply. The UUA is committed to developing a diverse and talented staff team. If you are excited about thisrole, butare unsure whether you meet 100% of the requirements, we encourage you to inquire and/or apply. Please submit your resume and cover letter via our applicant portal (ADPWorkforceNow)on uua.org/jobs.If you have any questions, please reach out .

About the UUA

The Unitarian Universalist Association is a progressive religious denomination headquartered in Boston’s waterfront Fort Point Innovation District. Our faith community of more than 1,000 self-governing congregations brings to the world a vision of religious freedom, tolerance, and social justice. Our normal workweek is 35 hours, we pay 80% contribution towards health insurance premiums, 10% towards retirement (after one year), and have generous paid time-off policies. We are a great place to work, and we value diversity. The UUA is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to the full inclusion of all. As part of this commitment, the UUA will ensure that applicants and staff with disabilities areprovidedreasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed toparticipatein the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please contact theDepartmentof Human Resources . For more information on the UUA, visit us online at UUA.org and uuworld.org.

Support for the Mission and Values of the Association

The Unitarian Universalist Association is a progressive and historic religious denomination. All UUA staff members are expected to perform their job duties in accordance with the UUA’s values, principles, and mission. Unitarian Universalism puts love at the center of our commitments, which embrace the Shared Values of justice, equity, transformation, interdependence, pluralism and generosity. The following points drawn from these Shared Values are of particular importance for the UUA’s work environment and staff culture:

  • Pluralism and generosity: We affirm the need for a human-centered workplace that allows our diverse staff to flourish. We also understand that our wider culture and society oppresses and denies human dignity, and we seek to counter the effects of that oppression in our hiring and workplace culture so that each person feels whole and valued.
  • Justice and equity: We speak openly and publicly of our support for social and political issues, including LGBTQ equity, racial justice, climate justice, gender equity, and reproductive justice.
  • Interdependence and transformation: We recognize that the liberation of all people is interwoven, and we work to counter patriarchy, white supremacy, colonialism, homophobia, transphobia, environmental exploitation, and other interrelated systems of marginalization.

Position Highlights

Position Title: Data Engineer

FLSA Classification: Exempt

Location: Remote; must be based in the United States. Up to 10% domestic travel may be required.

Salary Range: $103,500 - $143,500 annually, plus benefits. Individual salary offers will be based on experience and qualifications unique to each candidate.

Position Type: Grant-funded, limited-term opportunity

Position End Date: June 30, 2027

Overview

The Data Engineer will play a key role in advancing the CDC Foundation's mission by designing, building, and maintaining data infrastructure for a public health organization. This position supports the Workforce Acceleration Initiative (WAI), a federally funded CDC Foundation program dedicated to helping public health agencies accelerate information system improvements through technology and data expertise.

Working within the Chickasaw Nation Department of Health (CNDH), Division of Public Health, the Data Engineer will collaborate in planning and developing solutions for interoperable data generation, storage, processing, and analysis across systems supporting tribal public health operations. The role will partner closely with data content experts, analysts, data scientists, data modelers, data warehouse architects, IT professionals, and other organizational staff to design and implement scalable, sustainable solutions that meet agency needs.

In addition to technical responsibilities, the Data Engineer will provide training and mentorship to Division of Public Health staff to support capacity building and promote long-term system sustainability.

The Data Engineer will be employed by the CDC Foundation and assigned to the CNDH Division of Public Health. This position is eligible for a fully remote work arrangement for candidates based in the United States.

Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and maintain data systems and pipelines that support the efficient and reliable ingestion, processing, transformation, and storage of data.

  • Collect data from multiple sources; cleanse, transform, and validate data to ensure accuracy, consistency, and integrity before loading into data storage platforms and data warehouses.

  • Optimize data pipelines, infrastructure, and workflows to improve performance, efficiency, reliability, and scalability.

  • Monitor data pipelines and platforms for performance issues, errors, and anomalies, implementing corrective actions as needed.

  • Implement and maintain appropriate security controls and data governance practices to protect sensitive and confidential information.

  • Collaborate with data scientists, analysts, and business partners to understand data requirements and ensure data infrastructure supports organizational goals and objectives.

  • Partner with cross-functional teams to gather requirements and design scalable, sustainable data solutions that meet business and public health needs.

  • Develop, implement, and maintain ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) processes to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and consistency of organizational data.

  • Design and manage data storage solutions, including relational databases, NoSQL databases, and enterprise data warehouses.

  • Stay current on industry trends, best practices, and emerging technologies in data engineering, incorporating innovative solutions into the organization's data ecosystem.

  • Provide technical guidance, mentorship, and support to staff and project team members.

  • Communicate effectively with stakeholders at all organizational levels to gather requirements, provide project updates, and present technical solutions and findings.

  • Travel domestically up to 10% as needed to support project and partner engagement activities.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Data Science, or a related field required.

  • Minimum of five (5) years of relevant professional experience in data engineering, data architecture, or a related field.

  • Proficiency in programming languages commonly used in data engineering, including Python, R, Java, Scala, and SQL.

  • Demonstrated ability to develop scalable data automation solutions within established frameworks rather than relying on one-time scripting approaches.

  • Experience with big data technologies and frameworks, such as Hadoop, Spark, Kafka, and Flink.

  • Strong knowledge of database systems, including relational databases (e.g., MySQL, PostgreSQL) and NoSQL databases (e.g., MongoDB, Cassandra).

  • Experience working with large-scale or national datasets; experience with Epic Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems preferred.

  • Experience using data visualization tools, including Power BI.

  • Knowledge of software engineering best practices, including source control, automated testing, continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD), code review, and change management.

  • Strong understanding of data warehousing concepts, methodologies, and technologies.

  • Experience working with cloud computing platforms and cloud-native data solutions.

  • Expertise in data modeling, ETL development, data integration, and data lifecycle management.

  • Familiarity with Agile development methodologies, software design patterns, and modern development best practices.

  • Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to clearly communicate technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Ability to adapt to evolving priorities, deadlines, and project requirements.

  • Outstanding interpersonal and teamwork skills, with a demonstrated ability to build productive relationships with colleagues, partners, and stakeholders.

  • Experience working with tribal nations and tribal data sovereignty principles preferred.

  • Experience collaborating in remote and virtual work environments with geographically dispersed teams.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

  • Other duties as assigned.

Special Notes

This role is involved in a dynamic public health program. As such, roles and responsibilities are subject to change as situations evolve. Roles and responsibilities listed above may be expanded upon or updated to match priorities and needs, once written approval is received by the CDC Foundation to best support the public health programming.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, mental or physical disabilities, veteran status, and all other characteristics protected by law. We comply with all applicable laws, including E.O. 11246 and the Vietnam Era Readjustment Assistance Act of 1974, governing employment practices and do not discriminate on the basis of any unlawful criteria in accordance with 41 C.F.R. §§ 60-300.5(a)(12) and 60-741.5(a)(7). As a federal government contractor, we take affirmative action on behalf of protected veterans.

The CDC Foundation is a smoke-free environment

Relocation expenses are not included

About the CDC Foundation

The CDC Foundation is an independent nonprofit authorized by Congress to mobilize philanthropic partners to support the public health system, including the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), in preventing and responding to threats to health. In this role, we are focused on one priority: building catalytic, flexible and impactful partnerships—with corporations, philanthropies, individuals and organizations—to help improve the health and lives of people in all communities, everywhere. jobs.description:
Join Points of Light and Change the World

As the world’s largest organization dedicated to increasing volunteer service, Points of Light engages more than 3.8 million volunteers across 32 countries.

Cast from the vision of one thousand points of light shared by its founder, President George H.W. Bush, in his 1989 inaugural address, Points of Light was founded in 1990 as an independent, nonpartisan, nonprofit organization to encourage and empower the spirit of service. The organization extends President Bush’s vision that “any definition of a successful life must include serving others.” Today, Points of Light continues to transcend politics and borders to inspire millions of individuals worldwide to take action.

Join Us: Be part of a movement that changes lives and communities. Please read the position description below. For more information, visit pointsoflight.org.

Salary Range:$70,000-$80,000 annually

Reports to:Senior Director, Salesforce Platform & Governance

Department:Office of the Chief Operating Officer

Primary clients:Development and Business Development Revenue Teams

Location: Points of Light is a remote-first organization. Any U.S. location in the Eastern or Central time zone in a market with a major airport. Washington, DC preferred.

Position Summary: The Senior Manager, Customer Relationship Management (CRM) & Revenue Enablement leads Salesforce reporting and adoption work for Development and Business Development teams. This hands-on individual contributor brings business partners together around reporting questions and shared definitions, maintains trusted CRM views for consequential decisions, and leads approved revenue-CRM improvements from requirements through adoption. Revenue leaders define business priorities and own final interpretations; the Senior Manager prepares and checks initial analyses, flags limits in the data, and advises on the findings the evidence supports. During Awards planning, this role provides senior CRM and revenue enablement guidance to event leadership.

Position Functions and Responsibilities Include:

Revenue CRM Workflows and Data Stewardship

  • Lead the business-side improvement of Salesforce moves-management and earned-income workflows with Development and Business Development revenue leaders.
  • Lead business-side governance of agreed revenue-CRM definitions, quality checks and adoption standards; work with department leaders on recurring gaps in records their teams maintain.
  • Coordinate approved CRM data changes and workflow updates with identified source owners, validation steps and adoption measures.

Reporting Pipeline and Portfolio Enablement

  • Lead the design and maintenance of a reusable Salesforce reporting suite for pipeline, portfolios, proposals, sponsorships, fundraiser activity and other agreed revenue measures.
  • Convene revenue leaders to clarify the audiences, decisions and definitions behind complex reporting requests; build and check views that address those questions.
  • Prepare concise initial analysis of material changes and exceptions for recurring revenue and stewardship review, identify caveats, and help business leaders determine what requires further investigation.
  • Clarify the purpose, business owner, urgency, and scope of new CRM requests with sponsors; bring competing priorities to supervisor before committing team capacity.
  • Coordinate reporting definitions with Finance and Revenue and Grant Operations so CRM views align with official financial and agreement records.

Training Adoption and Client Support

  • Serve as a senior business-facing CRM adviser to Development and Business Development revenue teams, resolving complex process questions and improving the usability of recurring reports.
  • Design role-based training and self-service guidance with the Salesforce Super User network, and assess whether changes improve adoption and data quality.
  • Facilitate conversations across teams when inconsistent practices or definitions hinder accurate reporting.

Continuous Improvement and Platform Partnership

  • Propose and sequence a revenue-CRM enablement plan with the supervisor and revenue leaders, identifying dependencies and capacity tradeoffs.
  • Lead approved, time-bound revenue-CRM initiatives with defined sponsors, scope and success measures; guide requirements, testing, rollout and transition to routine support.
  • During Awards planning, serve as the senior CRM and revenue enablement partner to Development and event leadership; guide sponsorship workflows, reporting needs and cross-team handoffs, and lead resolution of CRM process issues while partnering with the supervisor on platform decisions.
  • Partner with the supervisor on platform design and releases and coordinate with the program enablement colleague where revenue and program information meet.
  • Take on other assigned work within CRM and revenue enablement, prioritized against the role’s core responsibilities.

Core Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Strong analytic judgment and the ability to explain data limitations and challenge unsupported conclusions constructively.
  • Ability to align senior business partners on definitions, priorities and feasible CRM solutions.
  • Advanced Salesforce reporting, data-quality and business analysis skills with a commitment to hands-on delivery.
  • Skill in leading scoped cross-functional work and building repeatable training and adoption practices.
  • Clear communication, sound prioritization and a service-oriented approach to collaboration.

Requirements:

  • At least five years of relevant CRM, fundraising operations or revenue enablement experience, including substantial hands-on Salesforce reporting, dashboards and data-quality analysis.
  • Expertise in leading a cross-functional CRM initiative from discovery through adoption and aligning stakeholders on measures and data definitions.
  • Working knowledge in data quality, user training, testing and explaining the limits of source data to decision-makers.
  • A bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience and the ability to create a welcoming work environment for all.
  • Proven track record of supporting a Development or fundraising team and working with donor, gift or pledge and stewardship data required; nonprofit fundraising and sponsorship experience strongly preferred.
  • Salesforce Administrator or Business Analyst certification strongly preferred.
  • Ability to create a welcoming work environment for all.

Culture and Values: Points of Light has a 35-year plus history that it seeks to honor, while looking toward the future as an innovative thought leader in the social sector. We have a fast-paced, collaborative environment. Our organization values innovation, dedication, teamwork and respectfulness. We enjoy thinking big, but also working hard to deliver our best work. Our team is solution-oriented, looking for someone who is always ready to deliver on ways to solve challenges, internally and with external partners.

What We Offer:Competitive compensation and excellent benefits including a robust PTO program: 18 days of PTO (increases to 20 days after three years of service) and 10 holidays; plus, we are closed December 25-January 1. Medical, dental and vision benefits offered, free life insurance, along with long-term and short-term disability, a 403(b) program with employer match, parental leave and one day of volunteer time off per month.

jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY

This position is responsible for the execution of revenue management processes and strategies that meet the company’s mission, standards and focus on continuous improvement, supporting the RMS Senior Leadership team to drive growth and results across the multi-brand portfolio.

SCOPE

Responsible for coordinating the revenue management functions (pricing, forecasting, competitive assessments, etc. as identified in assigned Core Deliverables) and inventory strategy for hotels supported by the RMS Team. Ensure hotels are priced appropriately and that inventory is allocated and restricted properly to ensure that revenue and profit are maximized.

Takes the lead in deployment of key MI initiatives and system changes and works to execute market-wide strategies or promotions by specific deadlines.

Provides revenue management functional expertise to designated hotels.

Location requirements: Contracted from London Regional Office however is a field-based role and therefore supports 100% remote working within the UK.

Language Requirements: High proficiency (speaking, reading and writing) in English is required. Multi language capability would be

viewed as a bonus given the international nature of the business.

Travel Requirements: Up to 20% business travel may be required.

CORE ACTIVITIES

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Expected Contributions

  • Responsible for coordinating the revenue management functions and inventory strategy for hotels across all brands, in alignment with agreed core deliverables.
  • Perform a range of tasks pertaining to the RM strategy of the hotel: training, analysis, auditing, research, report generation and software integration, including the preparation and initial analysis of weekly sales strategy packs.
  • Respond to, solve and make decisions on standard/routine business requests with limited risk.
  • Responsible for own work, with limited supervision following onboarding period, and contributing to team, department and/or business results.
  • Assist more senior associates in achieving business results by:
    • Utilizing technical knowledge and skills to enhance business processes.
      • Establishing priorities for self, and where appropriate, others.
      • Allocating own time effectively to meet goals in a manner that does not disadvantage other associates or groups.
      • Producing reports in response to internal and external requests for data.
  • Demonstrate an awareness of personal strengths and areas for improvement and act independently to improve and increase skills and knowledge.
  • Perform other duties as appropriate to the business.
  • Understand and deliver against MI revenue management initiatives and philosophies at all times.

Specific Expected Contributions (including duties and responsibilities)

  • Communicates and educates hotels on rational pricing, competitive positioning and restrictions and the impact that they may have on the hotels’ revenue strategies, whilst managing room authorizations, rates and restrictions. Effectively communicates brand specific revenue management philosophies as they pertain to One Yield recommended strategies.
  • Utilizes Marriott’s revenue management systems and tools to maximize revenue and profit for both transient and group segments, as required by the agreed Core Deliverables.
  • Prepares sales strategy meeting agenda and supporting documentation.
  • Conducts Sales Strategy meetings with General Manager and key property staff to educate and evaluate pricing and inventory strategies. Develops and implements strategies with the General Manager that will maintain and/or increase the hotel’s RevPAR.
  • Analyzes competitive performance using market share tools and shares recommendations for improvement with hotel teams.
  • Conducts remote system diagnostics audits and provide consistent recommendations.
  • Delivers training to various team members at contracted properties, ensuring hotel responsibilities are clear and manageable.
  • Executes pricing through High Performance Pricing, to include promotions, programs, and packages. Ensures compliance and participation in company promotions and digital channels, completing set up in HPP and eFast.
  • Ensures retail rates are evaluated through One Yield’s Retail Pricing Optimizer and updated based on changes in demand, product, or competitive positioning.
  • Ensures retail price parity is executed across all booking channels and ensure that the Hotel(s) sales strategies are effectively implemented in the reservation system and the inventory systems in a timely manner.
  • Ensures that technical questions relating to reservations and property management systems are escalated to the correct support desk in a timely manner. Assists hotels with pricing and provides input on business evaluation recommendations, if required in the assigned core deliverables.
  • Perform ad-hoc revenue tasks and analysis as directed by RMS Senior Leadership team.
  • Leads efforts to coordinate strategies between group sales offices, if required in the assigned core deliverables.
  • Conducts any analysis required to maximize room revenue and profit, in line with agreed service deliverables.
  • Analyzes reports and available information to make long-term pricing recommendations with brand initiatives as a key focus.
  • Critiques property performance weekly/monthly for Transient & Group segments for assigned hotel(s).
  • Prepares, communicates, and critiques weekly and monthly rooms projections, in line with agreed service deliverables.
  • Responsible for accurate execution of inventory management tasks.
  • Uses demand forecast and relevant data points to determine, implement and control selling strategies.
  • Drives compliance and participation in company promotions and digital channels.

CANDIDATE PROFILE

Education & EXPERIENCE

2-year degree from an accredited university in Business Administration, Finance and Accounting, Economics, Hotel and Restaurant Management, or related major. 3 years’ experience in the revenue management discipline.

SKILLS & KNOWLEDGE

Building Successful Relationships – is able to develop constructive and cooperative working relationships with others and maintain them over time.Develops and manages internal key stakeholder relationships Understands the distinction between managed and franchise owners/operators and is able to seamlessly provide support to all levels of the business.

Demonstrating Knowledge - Demonstrating knowledge of job-relevant issues, products, systems, and processes.

Executing on a Strategy - taking a predetermined strategy and supporting the execution of that strategy.

Communicating Information Timely - Informing and/or updating other team members on relevant information in a timely manner.

Generating and Delivering Accurate and Timely Results - Generating and providing accurate and timely results in the form of reports, presentations, etc.

Analytical/Critical Thinking - The ability to gather and organize information using a logical and systematic process.

Intermediate Computer Skills – Utilizing the internet for job related search and information. Intermediate or higher mastery level of Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint.

Job Specific Computer Skills – MS Office applications essential. Marriott systems (MARSHA, Opera PMS and Opera S&C, HPP, MarRFP, eFast, MRDW, One Yield) would be advantageous but not necessary.

Oral Comprehension - The ability to listen to and understand information and ideas presented through spoken words and sentences.

Writing - Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

Mathematics - Using mathematics to solve problems. The ability to add, subtract, multiply, or divide quickly and correctly.

COMPETENCIES

Leadership

  • Adaptability - Determines how change impacts self and others; displays flexibility in adjusting priorities; and communicates both the reasons for change and how it impacts the workplace.
  • Communication - Customizes approach to conveying complex information and ideas to others in a convincing and engaging manner; appropriately interprets verbal and non-verbal behavior; and models active listening to ensure understanding.
  • Problem Solving and Decision Making - Models and coaches others on breaking complex issues into manageable parts, identifying and evaluating alternatives and their implications before making decisions, and involving and gaining agreement from others when making key decisions.
  • Professional Demeanor - Exhibits behavioral styles that convey confidence and command respect from others; makes a good first impression and represents the company in alignment with its values.

Managing Execution

  • Building and Contributing to Teams - Leads and participates as a member of a team to move the team toward the completion of common goals while fostering cohesion and collaboration among team members.
  • Driving for Results - Sets high standards of performance for self and/or others; assumes responsibility for work objectives; initiates, focuses, and monitors the efforts of self and/or others toward the accomplishment goals; proactively takes action and goes beyond what is required.
  • Planning and Organizing - Gathers information and resources required to set a plan of action for self and/or others; prioritizes and arranges work requirements for self and/or others to accomplish goals and ensure work is completed.

Building Relationships

  • Coworker Relationships - Interacts with others in a way that builds openness, trust, and confidence in the pursuit of organizational goals and lasting relationships.
  • Customer Relationships - Develops and sustains relationships based on an understanding of customer needs and actions consistent with the company’s service standards.
  • Global Mindset - Supports employees and business partners with diverse styles, abilities, motivations, and/or cultural perspectives; utilizes differences to drive innovation, engagement and enhance business results; and ensures employees are given the opportunity to contribute to their full potential.

Generating Talent and Organizational Capability

  • Organizational Capability - Evaluates and adapts the structure of team assignments and work processes to best fit the needs and/or support the goals of an organizational unit.
  • Talent Management - Provides guidance and feedback to help individuals develop and strengthen skills and abilities needed to accomplish work objectives.

Learning and Applying Personal Expertise

  • Applied Learning - Seeks and makes the most of learning opportunities to improve performance of self and/or others.
  • Business Acumen - Understands and utilizes business information to manage everyday operations and generate innovative solutions to approach team, business, and administrative challenges.
  • Technical Acumen - Understands and utilizes professional skills and knowledge in a specific functional area to conduct and manage everyday business operations and generate innovative solutions to approach function-specific work challenges
    • Revenue Management - Knowledge of revenue management concepts, processes and strategies such as average daily rate, revenue per available room, sales cycles and trends, account management, pricing and inventory management. Skill in using a Yield Management system and interpreting pricing and inventory reports.
    • Analysis - The ability to analyze and summarize detailed data to make inferences and recommendations. Included is the creation and maintenance of spreadsheets for storing data.
    • Research - Skill in collecting information from a variety of sources relating to market data, historical cycles, travel and tourism trends, and real estate market dynamics. The ability to know when to seek additional information and where to look to find it.
    • Inventory Management - The ability to manage rooms and function space restrictions and thresholds using systems or manually in order to maximize revenue/profit across all segments.
    • Computer Skills - The willingness to learn and ability to use computer systems and software packages to input, access, modify, store, or output information or to execute programs and analyses. This includes the ability to enter and retrieve data from computer systems using a keyboard, mouse, or trackball.
    • Economics and Finance - Knowledge of economic principles and practices, P&L statements, operating budgets, forecasting and scheduling, and the reporting of financial data.
    • Sales and Marketing - Knowledge of sales and marketing concepts including principles and methods for showing, promoting and selling products or services as well as marketing strategies and tactics.
  • Basic Competencies - Fundamental competencies required for accomplishing basic work activities.
    • Basic Computer Skills - Uses basic computer hardware and software (e.g., personal computers, word processing software, Internet browsers, etc.).
    • Mathematical Reasoning - Demonstrates ability to add, subtract, multiply, or divide quickly, correctly, and in a way that allows one to solve work-related issues.
    • Oral Comprehension - Demonstrates ability to listen to and understand information and ideas presented through spoken words and sentences.
    • Reading Comprehension - Demonstrates understanding of written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.
    • Writing - Communicates effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

United Kingdom

At the time of application, applicants must have the legal right to work in the United Kingdom. Unfortunately, this role is not eligible for visa sponsorship or relocation assistance.

WHY JOIN MARRIOTT INTERNATIONAL?

Marriott International has been recognized as one of Fortune’s 100 Best Companies to Work For™ in 2026 by Great Place to Work®. This is a reflection of our people-first culture, commitment to wellbeing, and collaborative workplace. This accolade joins a growing list of regional honors, reinforcing our dedication to creating an exceptional environment where associates thrive.

We actively foster an environment where the unique backgrounds of our associates are valued and celebrated. Our greatest strength lies in the rich blend of culture, talent, and experiences of our associates. jobs.description:
About AWISEE

AWISEE is a fully remote international marketing agency working across Search, Social and AI Visibility for brands in technology, AI, fintech, gaming and consumer. Our team builds the internal products behind the agency: a creator data platform that scans more than 100,000 creator profiles a day, and the tools our influencer marketing team uses to match creators with brands and run campaigns. We are a small team that ships weekly and uses AI tools in everything we build.

Team: Influencer Marketing · Experience: 3–5 years · Type: Full-time · Work mode: Remote · Location: Mexico (LatAm)

About the role

You will make sure every influencer campaign we sell gets delivered: creators sourced, booked, briefed and live on time. Demand is not our problem. We run 15+ campaigns at once with new briefs arriving every week, and we need someone who owns fulfillment and internal coordination so campaigns ship without delays. You will work with the Head of Influencer Marketing, the campaign leads, the scouts and our AI Labs team.

What you will do

  • Own campaign delivery from kickoff to final report, across many campaigns in parallel.
  • Turn each client brief into a clear plan: creator numbers, markets, channels, deliverables, timeline and budget.
  • Make sure creator supply meets demand: get shortlists built and sent quickly, and keep booked creators moving.
  • Coordinate the work between campaign leads, scouts, contracts and finance so nothing waits on a handover.
  • Keep one up-to-date view of every campaign: status, blockers, deadlines and who owns the next step.
  • Follow up with clients on shortlist approvals, content approvals and feedback so campaigns do not stall.
  • Spot and fix risks early: creators dropping out, late content, missed posting dates.
  • Build and improve the team’s ways of working: checklists, templates and SOPs.
  • Help move the team from spreadsheets and email into our internal campaign hub, and give feedback to the developers building it.
  • Report on delivery: campaigns on time, creators booked versus needed, turnaround times.

Must have

  • 3+ years in influencer marketing, with hands-on campaign management at an agency or brand.
  • Experience running several campaigns at once across TikTok, Instagram and YouTube.
  • Strong operations and project management skills: you bring structure where there is none.
  • Experience sourcing, negotiating with and managing creators.
  • Clear, confident written and spoken English for client and creator communication.
  • Comfortable with data, trackers and AI tools in daily work.
  • Used to remote work across time zones.

Nice to have

  • Experience leading or coordinating a small team.
  • Experience with Twitch, Kick, X, podcasts or events.
  • Background in gaming, tech, AI or fintech campaigns.
  • Spanish or Portuguese.
  • Experience introducing a CRM or campaign tool to a team.

Compensation

USD 850 – 1,250 per month, full-time, fully remote.

How to apply

Apply through this posting with your CV and a short note on a campaign you delivered (size, creators, result).

Ready to be a Titan?

ServiceTitan is the leading software platform for the trades, powering the businesses that keep the world running. Our technology is our product, and the leaders who build it shape everything we ship. As the Lead Executive Recruiter, you will own the end-to-end search for ServiceTitan's most consequential technical leadership hires: Senior Director, VP, SVP, and confidential roles across Engineering, Product Management, and Design. You will serve as a trusted advisor to our most senior technology and product leaders, delivering not just candidates but market intelligence, competitive insight, and a point of view on a talent market where the best leaders are rarely looking. At ServiceTitan, Executive Recruiting is not a support function. It is a strategic driver of growth, and this role sits at the center of that.


You will report directly to the Global Head of Talent Acquisition and partner closely with our CTPO and R&D leadership to drive executive hiring. You'll join a 25+ person global TA team and serve as the point of excellence for executive search across Engineering, Product Management, and Design.


What You'll Do:

Own the R&D Executive Search Function

  • Lead full-cycle executive searches for Senior Director, VP, SVP, and proactive roles across Engineering, Product Management, and Design globally, from intake through offer close and onboarding handoff
  • Serve as the primary point of contact and strategic advisor to R&D hiring managers throughout each search
  • Design and execute bespoke search strategies for each role, including market mapping, target company lists, outreach sequencing, and candidate positioning
  • Manage a small portfolio of concurrent confidential searches with rigorous discretion and timeline discipline

Manufacturing is entering its biggest transformation in decades.

For years, we’ve helped manufacturers digitize their operations through a platform used by leading manufacturers across Europe and North America. From digital work instructions and quality management to traceability, skills and operational excellence, we’ve helped thousands of operators perform their work better, faster and safer.

But we’re only getting started.

The next generation of manufacturing won’t be driven by software alone. It will be powered by AI that fundamentally changes how work gets done on the factory floor. We’re not digitizing existing processes anymore. We’re redesigning manufacturing execution from the ground up.
Founded in 2016, Azumuta has grown into one of Europe’s leading Manufacturing SaaS scale-ups, working with some of the world’s most innovative manufacturers across industries including aerospace & defense, industrial machinery, automotive, electronics and medical devices.

We’re building what manufacturing will look like over the next decade. If that excites you, you’ll fit right in.

Ready to be part of the next steps?

Requirements

  • Are fluent in French (native) and professional in English.

  • Have experience in an outbound prospecting role (BDR/SDR), ideally in B2B SaaS industrial or technical sales.

  • Are structured, activity-driven and resilient: able to sustain a consistently high volume of touches without losing quality.

  • Are organized enough to work multiple sites and stakeholders within the same account in a structured way (CRM discipline), and to connect the dots across sites.

  • Are eager to learn: able to quickly grasp Azumuta 2.0 use cases and talk about them in plain language, no technical background required.

  • Are based in France or have strong knowledge of the French industrial market.

  • Be part of the future of manufacturing tech — Not just another job: you're joining a mission-driven scale-up ready to transform an entire industry.

  • Room to lead, space to grow — We give you autonomy, trust, and the freedom to shape your role, backed by training, mentorship, and continuous learning opportunities.

Location, Reporting & Travel

This is a fully remote role within the United States. Periodic travel (approximately 25–30%) will be required to conduct in-person meetings with members, support conferences and member engagement events, and attend internal team gatherings.

Reports to: Senior Director, Member Success, Academic

About Us

E3n is a not-for-profit, member-based organization serving independent schools, educators, students, and families across the full student lifecycle.

Formed through the merger of the former Educational Records Bureau (ERB) and the Enrollment Management Association (EMA), E3n builds on nearly a century of collective expertise in assessment, enrollment, and student development. E3n exists to deepen school impact and advance whole-student growth by uniting academic and enrollment leadership around shared, data-driven insights.

E3n provides comprehensive assessments, professional tools, conferences, and analytics that help independent schools demonstrate their value and support student success from pre-enrollment through graduation—extending beyond academic performance to include student well-being, sense of belonging, and social-emotional development.

About the Opportunity

The Director, Member Success, Academic, plays a key role in supporting E3n member schools and organizations in effectively using the organization's achievement assessments, student well-being tools, data resources, and professional learning offerings.

Working closely with the Senior Director, Member Success (Academic), this role manages relationships with a portfolio of member schools and helps ensure members experience meaningful value from their engagement with E3n. The Director serves as a trusted partner to academic leaders, providing guidance, support, and resources that help schools understand and apply assessment and student well-being data to strengthen teaching, learning, and student outcomes.

The Director collaborates with colleagues across the organization to ensure members receive timely support, successful onboarding experiences, and access to the resources they need to maximize the value of E3n's academic and student well-being tools and services. The role also plays an important part in identifying emerging member needs and sharing insights internally to strengthen E3n's products, services, and overall member experience.

The ideal candidate brings strong relationship management and consultative communication skills and is comfortable partnering directly with heads of school, academic deans, curriculum and instructional leaders, counselors, and other school-based educators. They are confident presenting to professional audiences, facilitating thoughtful conversations around assessment data and instructional improvement, and managing multiple member relationships in a dynamic environment. The successful candidate is motivated by helping schools translate data into meaningful action while serving as a trusted partner who brings member insights back to E3n to inform future products, services, and strategy.

What You’ll Do

Reporting to the Senior Director, Member Success (Academic), the Director is responsible for managing member relationships and supporting the success of schools within their assigned portfolio.

Member Relationship Management

  • Serve as the primary relationship manager for a portfolio of member schools.
  • Build and maintain trusted partnerships with heads of school, academic deans, curriculum leaders, division directors, counselors, and instructional leadership teams.
  • Act as a strategic partner, helping schools maximize the value of E3n's products and services.
  • Develop a deep understanding of each member's goals, priorities, and challenges while identifying opportunities to strengthen engagement and long-term partnership.

Member Onboarding & Engagement

  • Support onboarding of new members to ensure successful implementation of E3n's achievement assessments and related products and services..
  • Guide schools through effective use of assessment and student well-being tools, reporting platforms, and professional learning opportunities.
  • Facilitate ongoing engagement through regular member conversations focused on adoption, utilization, and member success.
  • Support opportunities to expand member engagement, including Associate-to-Full membership growth and additional product utilization as appropriate.

Member Support & Consultation

  • Partner with internal teams to respond to member questions and support requests in a timely manner.
  • Help schools interpret assessment results and connect insights to instructional planning and student success.
  • Coordinate with Product, Research, Professional Learning, and Platform teams to resolve member questions and improve the overall experience.
  • Ensure members receive practical guidance and resources that help them confidently leverage E3n's products and services.

Member Experience & Portfolio Insights

  • Monitor engagement across an assigned portfolio and identify opportunities to strengthen member success and retention.
  • Gather feedback from member schools and share insights to improve E3n's products, services, and member experience.
  • Identify emerging trends, challenges, and opportunities across member schools and communicate those insights internally.
  • Maintain accurate records and timely Salesforce records by documenting member interactions, engagement, opportunities, and support activities.
  • Monitor product utilization and proactively identify opportunities to deepen engagement.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with colleagues across Membership, Product, Research, Professional Learning, Growth, and Platform teams to deliver an exceptional member experience.
  • Contribute member insights that inform future products, services, research, and programming.
  • Support broader Member Success initiatives and organizational priorities.
  • Identify opportunities for product expansion or additional member engagement and collaborate with appropriate internal partners to support growth.

Member Engagement Activities

  • Represent E3n through conferences, webinars, workshops, and member-facing events.
  • Facilitate professional learning opportunities and discussions focused on assessment, instructional improvement, and student success.
  • Build relationships with prospective and existing member schools while representing the organization's mission and expertise.

Why Work with Us

At E3n, you’ll join a mission-driven organization formed through the unification of two respected leaders in independent education. We’re building something new—bringing together enrollment and academic perspectives to create deeper insight, stronger institutions, and better outcomes for students from pre-enrollment through graduation.

At E3n, you’ll experience:

  • Purpose with impact. Our work directly supports educators, school leaders, and families nationwide. The decisions we make—and the tools we build—matter.
  • Smart, thoughtful colleagues. You’ll work alongside people who care deeply about education, ask good questions, and value collaboration, clarity, and integrity.
  • Whole-person thinking. Just as we help schools understand the full student journey, we strive to support employees as whole people—recognizing that strong work is sustained by balance, trust, and belonging.
  • Growth during a moment of transformation. E3n is actively evolving. That means opportunities to shape systems, influence direction, and grow alongside an organization defining its future.
  • Values-driven, data-informed. We balance heart and rigor—grounding our work in evidence while staying anchored in empathy, equity, and real-world impact.

If you’re energized by meaningful work, thoughtful problem-solving, and helping schools better serve students, you’ll find a home at E3n.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • 9-12+ years of experience in education, academic leadership, assessment, member success, customer success, or relationship management.
  • Experience working with schools, educators, or education-focused organizations.

Preferred Skills & Experiences

  • Experience working within independent or private schools.
  • Experience supporting educators through assessment programs, educational data systems, or instructional improvement initiatives.
  • Background in teaching, curriculum development and planning, academic leadership, or educational assessment.
  • Experience presenting to professional audiences or facilitating workshops for educators and school leaders.
  • Experience in independent school admissions or enrollment management is a plus, particularly for candidates who also bring strong academic, teaching, or instructional leadership experience.

The ideal candidate has strong healthcare Revenue Cycle Management experience, prior team leadership or supervisory experience, and a thorough understanding of how intake, eligibility and benefits verification, prior authorization, scheduling, patient access, and reimbursement work together. Prior RCM experience supporting behavioral health services and fluency in both English and Spanish are required.

Key Responsibilities

Team Leadership and Daily Operations

  • Provide day-to-day leadership and direction to team members supporting Intake, Authorization, and Scheduling functions.
  • Coordinate daily workloads, assignments, priorities, and coverage to ensure operational requirements and service expectations are met.
  • Serve as the first point of escalation for workflow questions, complex cases, payer issues, patient access concerns, and other operational challenges.
  • Monitor team productivity, quality, attendance, responsiveness, and adherence to established processes.
  • Conduct regular team meetings, individual coaching sessions, and performance discussions.
  • Support onboarding and training of new team members and provide ongoing education as workflows, payer requirements, and client expectations change.
  • Identify performance gaps and provide appropriate coaching, retraining, and performance development to ensure consistent service delivery.
  • Promote accountability, collaboration, and consistent execution across the team.
  • Ensure staff consistently follow established client procedures, service expectations, and escalation protocols.

Training and Employee Development

  • Lead initial onboarding and training for newly hired intake coordinators and scheduling staff.
  • Ensure employees demonstrate a thorough understanding of assigned workflows, patient communication expectations, and client-specific procedures.
  • Evaluate employee knowledge, competency, and readiness before transitioning to independent patient interactions.
  • Provide ongoing refresher training and individualized coaching based on employee performance and quality findings.
  • Identify training gaps and collaborate with operational leadership to develop corrective training plans.
  • Reinforce appropriate communication techniques when interacting with patient experiencing emotional distress or sensitive behavioral health concerns.
  • Ensure employees understand established patient safety screening questions, escalation criteria, and warm-transfer procedures.
  • Maintain documentation of employee training, competency assessments, coaching, and development progress.
  • Collaborate with client representatives to ensure training aligns with established expectation and operational requirements.

Intake and Patient Access Oversight

  • Oversee intake and referral workflows to ensure patient demographic, insurance, referral, and required documentation is collected accurately and timely.
  • Ensure eligibility and benefits verification is completed appropriately before services are provided.
  • Monitor incomplete referrals and outstanding intake requirements and ensure appropriate follow-up occurs.
  • Support escalation of complex eligibility, coverage, referral, and patient access issues.
  • Ensure team members accurately identify and route prior authorization requirements during the intake process.
  • Reinforce compassionate, patient-centered communication throughout the intake process.
  • Ensure employees demonstrate active listening, empathy, professionalism, and sensitivity when interacting with behavioral health patients and their families.
  • Monitor adherence to established patient safety screening and escalation protocols.
  • Ensure appropriate escalation and warm transfer to designated clinical personnel when patient safety concerns are identified.
  • These responsibilities reflect the Intake Specialist workflow, which covers referrals, eligibility and benefits, authorization identification, scheduling coordination and front-end reimbursement readiness. RCM Intake Specialist RCM Intake Specialist

Authorization and Payer Management Oversight

  • Oversee prior authorization workflows, including eligibility verification, authorization submission, tracking, renewals, concurrent reviews, denial follow-up, and appeals.
  • Ensure authorization requests are complete, accurate, and submitted within applicable payer timelines.
  • Monitor pending and expiring authorizations and ensure appropriate follow-up occurs before services or authorized limits are impacted.
  • Support team members with complex payer requirements, authorization issues, denials, and escalations.
  • Monitor authorization-related denial trends and work with operational leadership to identify opportunities for process improvement.
  • Ensure accurate documentation of authorization numbers, approved services, effective dates, expiration dates, visit limits, and other payer requirements.
  • The underlying Authorization Specialist role specifically owns authorization submission and tracking, continued-stay reviews, denial follow-up, appeals and payer coordination, making this an important technical competency for the lead.

Scheduling and Capacity Oversight

  • Oversee ongoing patient scheduling, rescheduling, cancellations, no-show follow-up, waitlists, and appointment reminder workflows.
  • Ensure scheduling activity appropriately considers provider availability, service requirements, patient needs, and authorization status.
  • Monitor provider utilization and open appointment capacity and work with the team to minimize unfilled appointment slots.
  • Ensure pending, expired, or incomplete authorizations are identified before affected services are scheduled.
  • Support escalation of scheduling issues that may affect patient access, provider utilization, reimbursement, or continuity of care.
  • Monitor scheduling trends and work with operational leadership to address capacity constraints and recurring workflow issues.
  • The Scheduling Coordinator profile makes provider utilization, waitlists, authorization coordination and billing readiness core parts of that function, so I would absolutely include those in the lead's oversight. RCM Scheduling Coordinator

Performance, Quality and Reporting

  • Monitor team performance against established productivity, quality, accuracy, turnaround time, and service-level expectations.
  • Track and report key operational metrics across Intake, Authorization, and Scheduling functions.
  • Conduct routine call monitoring and quality audits to evaluate employee performance, accuracy, professionalism, empathy, and adherence to established workflows.
  • Assess patient interactions for effective communication, active listening, appropriate tone, and compassionate service delivery.
  • Identify trends, workflow gaps, recurring payer issues, and performance concerns and recommend corrective actions.
  • Provide timely, constructive coaching and feedback based on quality audit findings.
  • Assist management with reporting, workload forecasting, staffing needs, and resource allocation.
  • Maintain accurate documentation of team performance, coaching, training, and operational issues.
  • Support process improvement initiatives designed to improve patient access, authorization performance, scheduling efficiency, reimbursement readiness, and overall revenue cycle performance.

Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Serve as a liaison between Intake, Authorization, Scheduling, Billing, Clinical, and other revenue cycle and operational teams.
  • Collaborate with client representatives to ensure training, quality standards, and operational workflows align with established expectations.
  • Participate in client meetings, operational discussions, and quality improvement initiatives as needed.
  • Coordinate with designated clinical personnel to ensure appropriate handling and escalation of patient safety concerns.
  • Coordinate resolution of issues that cross multiple functions or could create reimbursement risk.
  • Communicate significant payer, workflow, staffing, or performance issues to management.
  • Support implementation of new processes, payer requirements, client procedures, and operational changes.
  • Maintain effective communication with client and internal stakeholders as appropriate.
  • Ensure consistent handoffs between Intake, Authorization, and Scheduling teams to reduce delays, errors, and avoidable reimbursement issues.

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum of 3 years of healthcare Revenue Cycle Management experience, with experience in patient access, intake, insurance verification, prior authorization, scheduling, or related front-end RCM functions.
  • Prior RCM experience supporting behavioral health services is required.
  • Fluency in English and Spanish, including the ability to communicate health insurance, eligibility, benefits, scheduling, and patient access information clearly and accurately in both languages.
  • Previous experience as a Team Lead, Senior Specialist, Supervisor, or similar role with responsibility for providing day-to-day direction to multiple team members.
  • Demonstrated experience training, coaching, and evaluating employee performance.
  • Strong understanding of insurance eligibility and benefits, prior authorization, payer requirements, patient access, scheduling, and their relationship to reimbursement.
  • Experience working with commercial and managed care payers.
  • Experience using payer portals such as Availity, NaviNet, and payer-specific platforms.
  • Experience with EHR, practice management, scheduling, or other healthcare revenue cycle systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to monitor productivity, quality, workload, and operational performance.
  • Strong coaching, communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and operational workflows in a high-volume environment.
  • Working knowledge of HIPAA and healthcare privacy and confidentiality requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Associate or bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, or a related field.
  • Experience directly supervising or leading teams across multiple front-end RCM functions.
  • Experience with behavioral health intake, authorization, and scheduling workflows.
  • Experience with authorization denials, appeals, concurrent review, and continued-stay processes.
  • Experience monitoring operational KPIs and preparing performance reports.
  • Experience supporting multi-provider, multi-location, or centralized revenue cycle operations.
  • Experience participating in quality assurance, training, workflow design, or process improvement initiatives.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Strong understanding of front-end healthcare revenue cycle operations from initial referral through authorization and ongoing scheduling.
  • Ability to effectively train, coach, mentor, and develop employees with varying levels of experience.
  • Strong quality assurance skills, including evaluating patient interactions, identifying performance gaps, and providing actionable feedback.
  • Ability to communicate fluently and accurately in both English and Spanish.
  • Understanding of appropriate patient safety screening, escalation, and warm-transfer procedures.
  • Strong people leadership and coaching skills.
  • Ability to prioritize and distribute work across multiple employees and functional areas.
  • Ability to identify and resolve operational issues before they affect patient access or reimbursement.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret performance trends and identify root causes.
  • Excellent attention to detail and commitment to documentation accuracy.
  • Ability to communicate payer and operational requirements clearly to team members.
  • Strong sense of urgency and ability to make sound decisions in a high-volume environment.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across clinical, operational, billing, authorization, scheduling, intake, and other revenue cycle teams.
